themes: Preserve raw sources, then compile durable knowledge
Use hybrid retrieval plus a human-readable knowledge graph
Treat benchmark quality, latency, and context tokens as separate metrics
Keep host-native lifecycle hooks instead of forcing one memory rhythm
Route memories through topic and subtopic paths so recall can boost the right branch
Supersede stale bug and task memories instead of letting old failures keep ranking
Expose dashboard-level health before zooming into clusters, paths, and documents

sources.title: Karpathy LLM Wiki pattern
sources.memoryImplication: Use immutable sources, an agent-maintained wiki, a schema file, index, log, and periodic lint so memory compounds instead of becoming only query-time RAG.
challenges: Needs guardrails to avoid stale compiled pages

sources.title: GBrain public repository
sources.memoryImplication: Add typed links, brain-first lookup, auto-linking on writes, background consolidation, and a doctor/remediation loop as inspiration, without copying private data or unverified claims.
challenges: Do not claim GBrain parity until compatible evals are run

sources.title: Karpathy LLM Wiki Obsidian plugin
sources.memoryImplication: Keep RecallWeave vault output Obsidian-compatible with wiki links, generated indexes, lint, duplicate detection, contradiction handling, and reviewed-page protection.
challenges: Native Brain UI should be cleaner for nontechnical users than raw Obsidian files

sources.title: MemoryBench public harness
sources.memoryImplication: Use checkpointed ingest, index, search, answer, evaluate, and report runs. Report accuracy, latency, and context tokens separately instead of one vague score.
challenges: Hosted Supermemory baseline is blocked until a non-quota-limited key is available

sources.title: Supermemory public repository
sources.memoryImplication: Mirror the useful public-facing behavior: profiles, hybrid search, contradiction handling, connectors, and easy host plugins, while keeping RecallWeave local writes separate.
challenges: Public claims about beating Supermemory require fresh matched baselines

sources.title: Hermes memory provider plugin docs
sources.memoryImplication: Use Hermes provider hooks for system prompt blocks, prefetch, queued prefetch, sync turn, session end, pre-compress preservation, and mirrored memory writes.
challenges: Only one external Hermes memory provider is active at a time

sources.title: Storage Is Not Memory
sources.memoryImplication: Preserve verbatim event substrate and defer some extraction until retrieval because facts discarded at ingest cannot be recovered later.
challenges: Benchmark claims are technical-report claims and need reproduction before product copy

sources.title: PlugMem task-agnostic memory module
sources.memoryImplication: Favor compact knowledge-centric graph memories for decision-relevant information instead of flooding prompts with raw trajectories.
challenges: Still keep raw evidence available for audit and retrieval fallback

sources.title: LongMemEval V2
sources.memoryImplication: Add tests for environment gotchas, workflow knowledge, dynamic state tracking, and premise awareness, not only preference recall.
challenges: Coding-agent evidence gathering can improve accuracy but may add latency

sources.title: EvoMemBench
sources.memoryImplication: Evaluate knowledge memory and execution memory separately because no single memory form wins across all settings.
challenges: Do not optimize one benchmark and claim general memory superiority

sources.title: MemoryArena
sources.memoryImplication: Add multi-session agent loops where memories are learned during action and reused later, because static recall benchmarks miss operational failures.
challenges: Requires controlled tasks beyond current fixture dashboard

implementationRules.label: Human-readable brain
implementationRules.decision: Translate memory internals into ideas, workflows, decisions, evidence, contradictions, and review state in the UI.

implementationRules.label: Raw plus compiled
implementationRules.decision: Preserve source substrate for audit while compiling concise wiki and graph knowledge for prompt-time recall.

implementationRules.label: Host-native lifecycle
implementationRules.decision: Use Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, and Claude lifecycle hooks natively, then map them into one RecallWeave container contract.

implementationRules.label: Separated benchmarks
implementationRules.decision: Track quality, latency, context tokens, privacy failures, and production-use failures as separate gates.

implementationRules.label: Topic paths
implementationRules.decision: Store major topic and subtopic paths on memories and wiki pages, then use those paths as graph links and retrieval boosts.

implementationRules.label: Stale memory supersession
implementationRules.decision: When a bug, task, or contradiction is resolved, add a superseding state and demote the stale open item while preserving the fix history.

implementationRules.label: Budgeted lifecycle frequency
implementationRules.decision: Expose user-adjustable recall and write cadence so agents can trade latency, token cost, and continuity instead of hardcoding one frequency.

implementationRules.label: Dashboard to cluster zoom
implementationRules.decision: Start with dashboard health and activity metrics, then let users zoom into topic clusters, linked paths, and editable documents as memory scale grows.

benchmarkTargets.label: Limited MemoryBench rerun
benchmarkTargets.reason: Needed before claiming Supermemory parity or superiority.

benchmarkTargets.label: One-agent live canary
benchmarkTargets.reason: Needed to prove prompt-time recall actually appears during work.

benchmarkTargets.label: Human Brain UI review
benchmarkTargets.reason: Needed to confirm the UI is readable without inspecting JSON.

caveats: This fixture source lock is public-safe and contains no private agent memory.
It does not prove current SOTA performance. It only constrains what RecallWeave should test and implement next.
GBrain and recent arXiv benchmark claims need reproduction before being used as marketing claims.
